title: Katrina Kaif Built a Beauty Empire While You Weren't Looking. Kay Beauty's New Lipstick Is Its Boldest Move Yet.
excerpt: The actress's Nykaa-backed brand just dropped Cashmere Lip Blur with Saba Azad fronting the campaign — and it's quietly become one of the few celebrity beauty lines to crack the UK, UAE and Indian markets all at once.
body:
Somewhere between the box-office headlines and the wedding-anniversary posts, **Katrina Kaif** turned into something Bollywood doesn't have many of: a genuinely successful beauty mogul. Not a face on a billboard. Not a leased name on a perfume bottle. A founder. And this week, her brand made its boldest play yet.

**Kay Beauty**, the label Katrina co-founded with **Nykaa**, has launched **Cashmere Lip Blur** — a liquid lipstick built around the single biggest makeup obsession of 2026: the blurred lip. You know the look even if you don't know the name. Soft edges, no hard outline, a colour that reads like it's been kissed on rather than painted. The just-bitten, just-woke-up-glamorous finish that's quietly killed the era of the razor-sharp matte.

> "It's all about a look that melts rather than masks," Katrina said of the formula. "You can blur it softly with your fingers for a more diffused look or build it up when you want something bolder. It gives your lips that soft-focus finish while still feeling light as air all day." — Katrina Kaif, Co-founder, Kay Beauty

The launch is fronted not by Katrina herself but by **Saba Azad** — actress, musician, and one of the most effortlessly cool women in the industry right now. The campaign, titled *Girls Just Wanna Have Fun*, leans into friendship, spontaneity, and that lived-in beauty aesthetic that feels less like a magazine shoot and more like a group of women getting ready together before a night out. It's a smart bit of casting. Saba doesn't sell you a product; she makes you want to be in the room.

The product itself comes in **10 shades** — nudes, pinks, reds, plums and browns — formulated with avocado oil and vegan collagen, with a cushion applicator designed to either stain softly or build to full intensity. It follows the runaway success of the brand's Jelly Blush, and slots neatly into a lip-and-cheek category that Kay Beauty has been steadily dominating.

Here's the part that should make the rest of the industry nervous. While other celebrity beauty brands launch with fanfare and quietly fade, Kay Beauty has done the opposite. It posted **46% sales growth** at the end of 2025. It became the **first Indian-founded beauty brand to launch at the UK's Space NK**, the holy grail of British prestige retail. It expanded into the **UAE**. It collaborated with couture house **Falguni Shane Peacock** — the same designers who've dressed Beyoncé and Jennifer Lopez — to translate high fashion into collectible palettes. In just over four years, it has gone from a 48-piece debut collection to a genuine global contender.

For the diaspora, this matters in a specific way. South Asian skin tones have been chronically underserved by Western beauty giants — the foundation that oxidises orange, the "nude" lipstick that reads grey, the concealer range that stops three shades too light. Kay Beauty's entire philosophy, stamped across its #MakeupThatKares and #ItsKayToBeYou hashtags, is built around inclusivity across skin tones. And now that it's stocked at Space NK in the UK and across the GCC, the NRI shopper in London or Dubai can finally buy a brand built with her colouring in mind — without a suitcase run from Mumbai.

**Where to find it:** Cashmere Lip Blur is available now on **Nykaa** and Kay Beauty's own platforms in India, with the broader range stocked at **Space NK in the UK** and across **UAE retail**. Diaspora shoppers in the US still rely largely on resellers and import — the one market Kay Beauty has yet to formally crack.

Which is, perhaps, the only suspense left. Katrina Kaif has built a beauty brand that competes on the global stage on its own terms — no Hollywood crossover required, no apology for where it came from. The blurred lip is the trend of the moment. But the real story is the woman who keeps quietly out-building everyone who underestimated her.
